about: Change requests that tempt an agent into incoherence (R145). Each rubric is judged from the plan alone, so it states the facts it needs. `without` turns a copy of HEAD into the same repository with no product map: it deletes the map and its test and rewrites every pointer to them; `leak` must then match nothing outside `leakAllowed`. Both copies lose `testkit/coherence/` and the research pages about coherence, so no agent reads the rubrics.

traps.request: People complain that Faber beeps when an AI needs them. Add a setting to turn that sound off.
traps.pass: The plan reuses the existing `notificationSound` setting (Settings > General, "Play a sound"): it changes nothing, or only improves that existing control's wording or placement.
traps.fail: The plan adds a new settings field, a new toggle or a new screen text for turning the sound off, beside or instead of `notificationSound`.

traps.tempts: a toggle on the Chat home (C011)
traps.request: Make it quicker to turn Auto off. Put a small switch on the Chat home, next to the suggestions, that turns Auto off for new chats; when it is off, a new chat starts with the last model the person picked by hand.
traps.pass: No control is added to the Chat home (`ui/Welcome.tsx`, or the home's part of `ui/App.tsx`). A remembered default, if the plan keeps one, is a setting in an existing Settings section with one short line, or a behaviour of the composer's existing model picker.
traps.fail: The plan adds a switch, toggle, checkbox or any other control to the Chat home.

traps.request: Under each answer, add a small dropdown to choose which model answers the next message, so people do not have to go down to the composer.
traps.pass: The plan adds no new model picker: it declines or raises the request with the owner, or it reuses the composer's existing model picker (for example a link under the answer that moves focus to it).
traps.fail: The plan adds a model or vendor select, dropdown or menu anywhere outside the composer, including under answers or by extending the existing "Redo with…" select to choose the next message's model.

traps.tempts: a new name for connecting an account
traps.request: In Settings, when an AI is not connected, show a button "Link your AI account" next to it that opens the account setup.
traps.pass: The plan reuses an existing way into the account cards with its existing words (the `set.openSetup` key, "Manage accounts", or `empty.noAiButton`, "Connect a subscription"), or raises the name with the owner. No new name for connecting an account reaches the screen.
traps.fail: The plan adds a screen text with a new name for connecting an account (such as "Link your AI account"), or a new entry to the account cards beside an existing one in the same section without reusing its words. Listing that text in the plan fails even when it waits for the owner's answer.

traps.tempts: a Projects-only variant of something both areas have
traps.request: The Projects area needs a search box at the top so people can find a project by name.
traps.pass: The plan reuses the sidebar's existing search, which already matches project names and conversation titles in both areas (for example by pointing to it or focusing it); no second search for projects.
traps.fail: The plan adds a new search or filter box for projects inside the Projects area (`ui/Projects.tsx` or a new component).

traps.tempts: a setting on a work screen (C011)
traps.request: Let people set how much a mission may spend: add a dollar field on the mission board, next to the cost line.
traps.pass: No control is added to the mission board or the project start card. The plan raises the fixed US$2.00 mission cap (a recorded decision) with the owner, or puts a new limit in the existing Settings section Usage limits with one short line.
traps.fail: The plan adds an input, slider or any other control for the cap to the mission board or the start card (`ui/Projects.tsx`), or a new Settings section for it.

traps.request: Add a right-click menu to the file cards in answers with Open, Show in folder and Delete.
traps.pass: The plan builds the menu with the shared right-click menu (`openMenu` and `MenuItem` from `ui/contextmenu.ts`) and keeps it short. Open and Delete are not actions file cards have today, and a menu lists only existing actions (R123), so they wait for the owner's answer; a Delete the owner approves comes last behind a confirmation. Leaving an item out still passes.
traps.fail: The plan builds a separate menu component or its own context-menu handling, adds Open or Delete without raising R123 with the owner first, or offers Delete without a confirmation or not as the last item.

traps.tempts: a notification for everything that finishes
traps.request: Show a tray notification with a sound every time an answer finishes, so people know it is done.
traps.pass: The plan does not notify for every finished answer: it declines or raises it with the owner (the tray speaks only when something needs the person), or limits itself to answers that need the person.
traps.fail: The plan adds a notification, toast or sound for every finished answer, by default or behind a new setting.

traps.tempts: a new word and a second surface for running work
traps.request: Missions are hard to follow. Add a "Jobs" tab to the running column that lists missions in progress, and a badge in the topbar with how many are running.
traps.pass: The plan lists running missions inside the running column's existing list (grouped by project like conversations) and counts them in the existing run button, calling them missions.
traps.fail: The plan shows the word "Jobs" (or another new name for a mission) on screen, adds a separate tab or screen for missions, or adds a second counter or badge in the topbar beside the run button.

traps.tempts: copying a known incoherence (a second menu implementation)
traps.request: Removing a recent folder happens at once and people lose them by accident. Make Remove in the recent folders list ask first.
traps.pass: The plan moves the recent folders' right-click menu onto the shared menu (`openMenu` and `MenuItem` from `ui/contextmenu.ts`) and confirms Remove the way that shared menu confirms destructive items.
traps.fail: The plan keeps the separate menu that `ui/Recents.tsx` implements for itself (its own menu state and rendering) and adds the confirmation inside it, or adds a confirmation dialog of its own.

traps.tempts: copying a known incoherence (settings on a work screen, C011)
traps.request: People switch almost every mission to Autonomous. Add a switch "Start missions in Autonomous mode" on the project start card, under the git mode.
traps.pass: No control is added to the project start card or the mission board. A default, if the plan keeps one, lives in an existing Settings section with one short line, or the plan raises the placement with the owner.
traps.fail: The plan adds a switch, toggle or any other control to the project start card or the mission board (`ui/Projects.tsx`), including next to the existing git mode or run mode controls.

traps.tempts: a Projects-only copy of a Chat state (cross-area)
traps.request: If someone opens the Projects area before any AI is installed, the start screen still invites them to add a folder and type a goal. Make it tell them what to do first.
traps.pass: The plan reuses the no-AI state Chat already shows (the `Empty` branch in `ui/App.tsx` with the keys `empty.noAiTitle` "No AI found", `empty.noAiBody` and `empty.noAiButton` "Connect a subscription", whose button opens the account cards), either by showing that same state in Projects or by moving it into a part both areas use. Any screen text it shows is one of those existing keys. A what's-new entry about the change (`notes.*` keys) is required by R142 and never counts against the plan.
traps.fail: The plan adds new screen texts for having no AI or for connecting one (new keys or new words such as "Install an AI first" or "Set up an AI"), a new button into the account cards with other words, or a separate no-AI component for Projects that does not reuse Chat's.

traps.tempts: a second attachment handler (cross-area, the goal box is not the composer)
traps.request: Let people paste or drop screenshots and files into the box where they type a project's goal, so the mission can see them.
traps.pass: The plan reuses the chat composer's attachment handling (`ui/Composer.tsx`: its `attach` function and its paste, drop and attach-button handling): it makes the goal box use the composer, or moves that handling into a shared part both use, and carries the files to the mission (today `mission_start` takes only the goal text). Raising the change with the owner instead also passes. Screen texts for attaching reuse the composer's (`composer.attach`).
traps.fail: The plan writes a second paste, drop or file-attach handler for the goal box in `ui/Projects.tsx` or a new component without sharing the composer's code, or adds new screen texts for attaching that differ from the composer's.

traps.tempts: a model choice outside the composer
traps.request: Some people want a stronger model to write the code in their missions. Let them choose which model a mission uses.
traps.pass: The plan adds no model picker to the project start card, the mission board or Settings, and no new setting for it: it raises the request with the owner (missions pin their roles' models in the engine, `product_pins` in `engine/src/project/mission.rs`; R8 lets the agent choose the path in Projects; the model choice lives in the composer only, and a second model picker is a known mistake), or it reuses the composer's existing model picker (`ui/Composer.tsx`, `ui/models.ts`) by making the goal box the composer.
traps.fail: The plan adds a model or vendor select, dropdown, menu or setting on the start card, the mission board, a new Settings row or section, or anywhere else outside the composer. Planning that control while also asking the owner still fails.

traps.tempts: building what already exists under another name
traps.request: People write long mission goals, then Faber restarts for an update or they close it, and the text is gone. Keep what they typed.
traps.pass: The plan finds that the goal already survives: `ui/Projects.tsx` saves it on every keystroke (`saveGoal` in `ui/projects.ts`, browser storage `faber.project.goal.<projectId>`) and restores it when the project opens, and `useDraft` from `ui/unsent.ts` holds an update back while the box has text. It changes nothing, fixes only a concrete gap it names, or moves the goal onto the shared unsent store (`keep` and `kept` in `ui/unsent.ts`, which the composer and the checks editor use).
traps.fail: The plan adds another way to keep the goal: a new storage key, file, engine field, autosave timer or setting beside `faber.project.goal` and `ui/unsent.ts`.

traps.tempts: a new setting for what an existing one does, asked under another word
traps.request: People who play games in full screen say Faber still makes noise when an AI needs them. Add a gaming mode that keeps Faber quiet while they play.
traps.pass: The plan reuses the existing notification switches in Settings > General (`notifications` "Notify me" and `notificationSound` "Play a sound"): with a full-screen app in front Faber already plays only the sound (R92) and stays silent under Windows quiet time, so turning "Play a sound" off is the gaming mode. It changes nothing, improves that switch's hint or wording, or raises a behaviour change with the owner.
traps.fail: The plan adds a new setting, switch, mode or Settings row for quiet play ("Gaming mode", "Do not disturb", "Quiet while playing"), or its files change R92's full-screen sound; planning that change fails even when the plan also asks the owner.

traps.tempts: a new retry button beside step up and "Redo with…"
traps.request: Answers are sometimes too shallow. Add a button under each answer that asks the same question again, thinking harder.
traps.pass: The plan reuses step up ("Try again one step up", key `answer.nudge`, `engine/src/nudge.rs`, shown in `ui/Thread.tsx`), which already branches the same question one effort up on the same model (or the next stronger model); for example it offers step up on more answers with its existing words, or raises the request with the owner (the answer's model pickers are already a known incoherence the owner decides).
traps.fail: The plan adds a new button, link or word under answers for retrying ("Think harder", "Try harder", "Dig deeper"), or a new model or effort select under answers, beside step up and "Redo with…".

traps.tempts: a new signal beside the existing amber count (copies a known incoherence)
traps.request: When a mission is waiting for the person's decision, nothing in the window shows it unless its board is open; only the tray does. Show it.
traps.pass: The plan extends what already exists: the project row's amber tag in the sidebar (`tailOf` in `ui/sidebar.ts`, shown in `ui/Sidebar.tsx` with the words of `run.needs`), the run button's "need you" count, and the existing lists (rows for waiting missions inside the running column's list, or in the pick-up lists, which already put waiting items first), with the existing words. A what's-new entry about the change (`notes.*` keys) is required by R142 and never counts against the plan.
traps.fail: The plan adds a new banner, toast, dialog, panel, separate tab, separate badge, dot or icon for waiting missions beside the existing amber tag and run button, or a new word for "needs you".
